text:
You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: The greet flow for customer "Ada" returns a generic welcome like "Welcome to Northwind Supplies!" that never uses her name. Other customers get the same nameless greeting. I expected a one-sentence welcome that addresses the customer by name.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.
I should start by exploring the project directory at /reeval/workspace to see what's there.
I'll start by locating the Genkit app and the greet flow.

text: The greet flow loads a dotprompt file, so the bug is likely in `prompts/greet.prompt`.

input.command: cat -A prompts/greet.prompt; echo ---; cat src/ai.ts; echo ---; cat src/index.ts
input.description: Show greet prompt with line endings and AI setup

text: Found it — the prompt template has `custmerName` misspelled instead of `customerName`, so Handlebars can't match it to the input and renders it blank, leaving a broken sentence that causes the model to fall back to a generic welcome message.
The template uses `{{custmerName}}` (typo) while the input schema and flow pass `customerName`. Fixing the placeholder.

input.command: node -e "const H=require('handlebars'); console.log(JSON.stringify(H.compile('named {{custmerName}}.')({customerName:'Ada'})))" 2>&1 | head -5; ls node_modules | grep -i handlebars

text: This confirms the typo causes the name to render blank, so the greeting ends up saying "named ." with nothing filled in. I'll write up the answer now, citing the broken line exactly as it appears and noting the file path as "prompts/greet.prompt" relative to the project root.
Handlebars renders the misspelled variable as an empty string, which confirms the cause. Writing `answer.json` now.

The root cause was a typo in the greet prompt template. `prompts/greet.prompt` used `{{custmerName}}`, but the input field is `customerName`. Handlebars rendered the missing variable as an empty string, so the model got no name and produced the generic welcome.

I changed the placeholder to `{{customerName}}`. Rendering the old template with `customerName: 'Ada'` gave `named .`, which confirms the cause. I wrote `answer.json` to the project root and did not touch `package.json` or add dependencies. I did not run the flow end to end against the model, so the fix is verified at the template-rendering level only.
